claims.text: Source-2 states: “\(I_{r,n-r}\) spanned by all \(s_\lambda\) with \(\lambda\not\subseteq(n-r)^r\) forms an ideal” and gives basis \(\{s_\lambda:\lambda\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2@L1318-L1330|claim=formal-document]

groundings.excerpt:
1318: The $\ZZ$-basis for $\Lambda$ given by the Schur functions $s_\lambda$ 
1319: has the property that the $\ZZ$-submodule $I_{r,n-r}$ spanned by all $s_\lambda$
1320: with  $\lambda \not\subseteq (n-r)^r$ forms an ideal, and the
1321: map sending $s_\lambda$ to $s_\lambda(x_1,\ldots,x_r)$ induces an isomorphism
1322: $$
1323: \Lambda/I_{r,n-r} \quad \overset{\sim}{\longrightarrow} \quad \ZZ[\xx]^{W_J}/\ZZ[\xx]^W_+ \ZZ[\xx]^{W_J} 
1324:                      \quad \left( \cong H^\star(G/P_J,\ZZ) \right) 
1325: $$
1326: Thus $H^\star(G/P_J,\ZZ)$ has $\ZZ$-basis given by 
1327: $$
1328: \{ \sigma_w: w \in W^J \}
1329: %  =   \{ \schubp_w: w \in W \text{ is }r-\text{grassmannian} \}
1330:   = \{s_\lambda: \lambda \subseteq (n-r)^r \}.

claims.text: Source-2 states: “\(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) is generated as an ideal of \(\Lambda/I_{r,n-r}\) by” \(\{s_\mu:i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq(n-r)^r\}\). [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]

The inspected bounded source passage defines an ambient box basis and an ideal generating set only; it does not explicitly define a presentation’s columns by \(i^j\subseteq\mu\subseteq q^r\), nor state that its complete \(h_1\)-relation rows are all \(h_1s_\lambda\) for corresponding interval-indexed \(\lambda\). [source-2@L1318-L1330|claim=formal-document] [source-2@L1365-L1375|claim=formal-document]
